Two sidebar plugins already cover most of these use cases today:

- **opencode-visual-cache** — main-session token breakdown (input/output/cache/system),
  per-model pricing, slash commands for settings.
  https://github.com/Hotakus/opencode-visual-cache
- **opencode-cache-hit** — cache hit rate, token totals, cost in multiple currencies,
  sub-agent rollup (child sessions), optional JSONL timeline export.
  https://github.com/zhumengzhu/opencode-cache-hit

Both read from `api.state.session`, so the data pipeline is already established —
no new tracking logic needed on the OpenCode side.

The `check-duplicates` failure appears to come from the duplicate PR workflow itself rather than this PR code.

Relevant log:

```text
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'session.data.id')
at script/duplicate-pr.ts:64:29
```

The failing step is:

```bash
COMMENT=$(bun script/duplicate-pr.ts -f pr_info.txt "Check the attached file for PR details and search for duplicates")
```

So `opencode.client.session.create()` returned without `data`, and `duplicate-pr.ts` crashes when accessing `session.data!.id`. This job runs from the base repo workflow/script and uses `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, so it is independent of the changes in this PR. Please rerun after fixing the workflow/API issue or review this PR manually.

Page Up/Page Down already have keyboard-independent alternatives: ctrl+alt+b scrolls up and ctrl+alt+f scrolls down. You can remap them in ~/.config/opencode/tui.json using messages_page_up and messages_page_down.

There is also a messages_last action, defaulting to ctrl+alt+g and End, which jumps directly to the bottom. However, that action currently only runs when the prompt editor is not focused. So remapping solves page scrolling, but a one-key jump to the absolute bottom while editing would still require a small behavior change.

You're right — I was mutating historical messages via a plugin, so I was breaking the prompt cache myself. The byte-identity framing here is wrong: Anthropic's cache is content-based, not object-identity-based, so a plain DB reload that produces identical content wouldn't break it.

The only real remnant is a minor perf angle — `filterCompactedEffect` does a full message-table reload on every loop iteration even when nothing changed — but that's redundant DB I/O at most, not a cache-correctness issue, and it overlaps with #24841 / #22208 anyway.

Closing this. Apologies for the noise.
